paragraphs: Rabbi Marinus (a Tanna of a baraita).

He is mentioned in Ketubot 60a: "It was taught: Rabbi Marinus says, a person suffering chest pain may suck milk on Shabbat," and in Niddah 37a: "It was taught: Rabbi Marinus says, there is no birth, etc." And in the Tosefta, Tahorot ch. 7: "He entered a valley in the rainy season, and impurity was [reported] in a certain field. They said before Rabbi Eliezer: it is the property of an individual." Rabbi Marinus explained in his name: [this applies to] any [field] that has a name of its own.

And the Tosefta is cited in abbreviated form in Bava Batra 56a. And Rashbam’s commentary explained "Rabbi Marinus in the name of Rabbi Yohanan," and from this the author of Seder HaDorot concluded that he was a student of Rabbi Yohanan. Hyman counters that in truth he is [cited in] a Tosefta and was a Tanna.

Hyman regards it as explicit in the Jerusalem Talmud, Shevuot ch. 6, halakhah 2, that he lived in the time of Rabbi [Yehuda ha-Nasi], for they say there: Rabbi Marinus stood surety for his daughter-in-law before the judges; Rabbi Hama, father of Rabbi Hoshaya, and Bar Kappara — and they asked Rabbi Hiyya the Great, and Rabbi Hiyya asked Rabbi.

And we find that he had a son named Shabbetai, as stated in Bava Metzia 17a: "Like the case of Shabbetai son of Rabbi Marinus, who wrote for his daughter-in-law a garment of fine cloth — he came before Rabbi Hiyya, etc."

notes.text: Goneach in the named Ketubot60a rule refers to a person in pain sucking milk on Shabbat. Hyman uses the Tosefta occurrence to reject Seder HaDorot’s inference from Rashbam that Marinus studied under Rabbi Yochanan. His chronology and family account remain attributed.

Machon Mamre Tosefta Tahorot 7:4 directly has Marinus explaining Eliezer’s ruling. Rashbam on Bava Batra 56a directly says Marinus spoke in Yochanan’s name. The consulted Guggenheimer Shevuot 6:2 has רבי חמא אבי בר קפרא ורבי הושעיה, differing from Hyman’s Chama father-of-Hoshaya and Bar Kappara sequence; the supplied wording is retained. Bava Metzia 17a directly names Shabbetai son of Marinus, his daughter-in-law’s garment and the appearance before Chiyya. Hyman’s reconciliation and chronology remain his, without merging these occurrences into a new identity record.
